headline: The Indonesia long-form drew more views on its seventh day than on its fourth and is close to becoming the channel's fifth breakout, so its Bali follow-up stays first. Today is the last day for the Guru Tegh Bahadur Short: write it tonight or press Drop, and give tomorrow to Churchill, due in four days with nothing written.

top3.topic: Sati ban, 4 December, and the Ayodhya stone, 6 December
top3.signal: Both Shorts are already written. “The Year Britain Banned Sati, Englishmen Were Selling Their Wives” is sourced and not recorded; the second Irfan Habib Short, on the Treta-ka-Thakur inscription, was written on 1 November.
top3.recommendation: The Tegh Bahadur slot opens tomorrow; the Sati Short should take it because it is written. Record by 2 December and publish the morning of 4 December, after settling the “never wrote a law” line the script itself flags. Then the inscription Short on the morning of 6 December.

top3.topic: 14 December 1971: the killing of Bengal's intellectuals
top3.signal: Eighteen days out, two days before Vijay Diwas. The planning step falls on 30 November. The channel's 1971 heli-bridge Short is one of its best subscriber-earners among Shorts.
top3.recommendation: Research this week who drew up the list and who carried it out, with names and the date; script a Short for the morning of 14 December. The channel's own failed 1971 refugee video left this lesson: “When the claim that makes the video unique is a cover-up, it goes in the first sentence, not at 60 percent.”

top3.topic: Two big films open on 4 December
top3.signal: Eetha, a biopic with Shraddha Kapoor, and Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace, a war film with Salman Khan, both with trailers out. What either one is about is not confirmed in today's data. A third, Baba, is listed as historical but is unverified.
top3.recommendation: Tomorrow, check what each film is about. If one tells a real event with a culprit who wronged Indians, script one Short on what the film leaves out, for 5 to 13 December: one person or one mystery, the villain in sentence one, about two minutes long to bring subscribers, judged on day three. If neither does, skip both. Three of the channel's four breakouts came from one film's release window.

skipped.signal: His Wikipedia readership is 24.77x its usual in Hindi and 9.18x in English, and his name is trending on X. The festival has passed.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. A saint's life story is the kind of Short that does poorly here, and the date is gone. Do not read this spike as demand for the Tegh Bahadur Short either.

skipped.topic: The Tipu Sultan row in Latur
skipped.signal: Still in the news: a Congress MLA's remarks, a BJP protest, an FIR over a defaced poster, and his descendant asking for the textbook chapter back.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. It is a party fight now, and party-politics Shorts do worst here; the Sonia Gandhi Short has no subscribers. The Tipu decision lapsed on 24 November; do not reopen it for this.

whats_working: “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” is holding: it drew more views on its seventh day than on its fourth and pushed long-form views up 161.8% week over week. Over 28 days long-form earns 86.4% of the net subscribers videos bring; over the 365-day window, 82.9%, at 7.49x as many subscribers per view as Shorts.

The best subscriber-earner of the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, 12.4 net per 1,000 views: a villain convicted by his own paycheck. The Churchill Short is built the same way.

The two Shorts since the film run are liked well above the usual Short: “How British Officers Lived Like Kings on Indian Land Tax” at 8.0% and “Why Portuguese Goa Taxed Every Hindu's SHIKHA” at 6.2%, against 3.9% for the median Short. Colonial tax stories land with the viewers who see them.
whats_wrong: Viewers leave the Indonesia long-form early: average view is 27.7%, and the biggest drop comes at 0:19, where 16 points of the audience go. What is said there cannot be read, because its transcript is still not in the library. Only 41.6% of November's long-form views were engaged views, and over the 365-day window long-form now brings 7.2 subscribers per 1,000 views, below its usual range. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing, and an opening that has not reached its culprit by 0:19. Test: read the line at 0:19 once the transcript is in; the Bali script names its culprit before then.

Shorts views fell 84.3% week over week (21,353 against 136,189). That is the film run ending, not new Shorts failing: the two posted since 22 November are at the channel's usual. It also changed where Shorts are found: search now brings only 32.2% of Shorts views over 28 days, under half. Test, still open: the Malay Ravana Short is not up yet; if its first day runs slower than the Goa shikha Short's 33.4 views an hour, no more film Shorts.

A viewer's fact-check under the Indonesia video says several supporting facts are wrong and questions the main argument, that sultans deliberately rewrote the Ramayana. Probable cause: the script leaned on one Malay text for a claim about intent. Test: answer it with sources this week; if a point is wrong, pin the correction before the Bali video goes up, because it goes to the same viewers.

“Why Sonia Gandhi NEVER Forgave Narasimha Rao” has 1,000 views and no subscribers, below the usual for its kind, even though viewers stayed (80.6% average view). Probable cause: party politics, the kind of Short that does worst here. No test needed; it is why the Tipu row below is a skip.

actions.action: Upload the Malay Ravana Short today: title starting “Ravana”, Related video set to the Indonesia long-form, its link in the pinned comment, and the text named on screen as the Malay “Hikayat Seri Rama”.
actions.rationale: It has been written since 19 November and exists to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form while that video still draws them. Each day it waits, that audience is smaller. Whether a Short sends viewers on is a guess.

actions.action: Answer the fact-check comment under the Indonesia video with sources (/replies drafts it), and pin a correction if any point is wrong.
actions.rationale: The Bali video goes to the same viewers; a fix made before it protects it.

actions.action: Test a new title and the designer's thumbnail on “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps” in Studio's Test & Compare.
actions.rationale: Over the 365-day window it brings 34.3 subscribers per 1,000 views, the best on the channel, on only 1,079 views. That the title is the reason is a guess.

actions.action: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” has 22 views since 3 November, and set GA4_PROPERTY_ID in .env so the brief can read itiha.info.
actions.rationale: A public Short gets a few views a day, so this points to a setting, not the topic. Without the Analytics id, the site shows only its brand-name searches.

growth.verdict: Needs 224 net subscribers a day. The channel does 67.73/day, so the target is a **3.3x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "1. Current rate, nothing changes"), reaches 67.7/day — still 3.3x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2030-03-15, 3.3 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1282 of the 3,291 subscribers that 22 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 30.8/day (863 of 1,761 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 22 long-form and 106 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.7 more long-form videos a year — 39.7 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 33 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 150, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 452 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 30.8/day (863 of 1,761 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 9 revision long-form videos, median 69 subscribers, against 33 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 30.8/day (863 of 1,761 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,282 subscribers on 73,144 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
